To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
lamb carcasses lose water in cold storage at a constant rate until the carcasses are at least 10% lighter.

the most important factor affecting frozen carcass losses is the heterogeneity of temperature in the freezer, which is caused by lighting, insulation, and poor airflow; that the rate of frozen carcass loss is greater in lean carcasses than in fat carcasses; and that the temperature at which carcasses are held has a significant effect on the rate of loss but in practice this is often outweighed by the effects of the heterogeneity of temperatures.
the most important factor affecting weight losses in frozen lamb carcasses is the local temperature within a freezer, which is caused by lighting, inadequate insulation and poor air movement.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effect of storage conditions on the weight loss of frozen lamb.
the loss in weight of lamb carcasses in frozen storage.
the effect of the environment on the weight loss from frozen meat.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the weight loss from carcass lamb stored in a cold store is a function of time of storage, the temperature of the cold store and the temperature of the air surrounding the carcasses.

lamb carcass weight loss during frozen storage is influenced primarily by the heterogeneity of temperature within the store, which is in turn affected by the design of the store, its age and the way in which it is operated.

lamb carcass losses in storage are a function of the following factors: (1) carcass fat content (2) storage temperature (3) storage time (4) air movement (5) temperature gradients (6) carcass weight (7) carcass shape (8) carcass wrapping.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the weight loss in lamb carcasses is very variable, and that the most important factors are the temperature variations inside the store and the time in store.
carcass losses in lamb are mainly caused by the presence of hot-spots in the cold store.
the main factors influencing frozen carcass losses are the temperature variations within an insulated store, the temperature level of storage and the fatness of the carcass.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the most significant factors affecting weight loss are: 1) temperature variations in the storage area caused by lighting, poor insulation and air flow, and 2) the age of the building.
the temperature of the storage facility is a critical factor influencing the rate at which weight is lost by frozen carcasses.
the temperature of the lamb carcass is not a very important factor influencing moisture loss.
